BLOCKER: No atomicity or idempotency guarantee for `finalize_item` writes; a crash mid‑write can leave a partial `final_report`, breaking the completion guard and requiring manual intervention.
MAJOR: No explicit definition of the `ac_hash` algorithm or staleness detection logic; risk of false `FINAL_REPORT_STALE` failures.
No concurrency control (locking/versioning) for `finalize_item`; concurrent runs could race and duplicate or overwrite `final_report`.
HIL approval verification lacks an explicit authentication/authorization mechanism; approvals could be spoofed or forged.
Ownership separation between the reviewer tool (findings) and main‑thread (dispositions) is not explicitly defined, risking a violation of CL‑002.
No backfill or grandfathering mechanism for existing items lacking `ac_verification`/`final_report`; only a timestamp‑based exemption is described, with no migration script or detection logic.
Semantics of “review markers”, “no‑review cache”, and “pre‑merge blocked set” are undefined, leading to inconsistent caching and gate behavior.
MINOR: No explicit definition of the “delta re‑review with prior findings” scope; prior findings could be missed.
No explicit definition of the “design pack + first‑pass quality contract” enforcement criteria.
Test classification categories beyond the listed kinds are undefined, risking misclassification of new test types.
No explicit definition of `cost_source` fallback precedence, potentially causing incorrect cost calculation.
No explicit definition of the rendering logic for `execution trail show`, risking inconsistent output across versions.
NIT: No explicit definition of the `review‑sha integrity` validation algorithm.
No explicit expiration policy for the “no‑review cache”.
No explicit ordering guarantee for the “pre‑merge blocked set”.
No explicit trigger conditions for “delta re‑review with prior findings”.
No explicit metrics for the “design pack + first‑pass quality contract”.
SUMMARY: Overall the design is comprehensive but lacks explicit definitions for critical mechanisms (`ac_hash`, concurrency, HIL verification, ownership separation).
Key risks include partial writes, false stale detection, and potential spoofing of approvals.
Clarify atomicity, concurrency control, and HIL verification before implementation.
